WHAT: A network design where the concept of a single cell tower is removed.
HOW: It distributes thousands of antennas across building walls and ceilings to surround users.
WHY: It creates a ubiquitous tracking grid where no "dead zones" exist to escape connectivity.

WHAT: The consolidation of radio network processing into central cloud servers.
HOW: It moves decision-making away from the device and into a central corporate cloud.
WHY: It concentrates power over global communications into the hands of a few tech giants.

WHAT: A radar-like capability built into the 6G network to map physical environments.
HOW: It uses radio wave reflections to detect the shape; speed; and position of objects and people.
WHY: It allows the network to "see" inside private homes without using optical cameras.

WHAT: An AI-driven system that autonomously manages radio spectrum rights.
HOW: It uses machine learning to decide which users or devices get priority access to bandwidth.
WHY: It removes human oversight; potentially prioritizing corporate traffic over civil needs.

WHAT: A security method that constantly verifies a user's identity in real-time.
HOW: It monitors behavioral biometrics like your walking gait; heartbeat; and typing rhythm 24/7.
WHY: It eliminates anonymity; treating every human movement as a biological login credential.

WHAT: The deep integration of digital algorithms with physical machinery and bodies.
HOW: It allows software codes to directly control physical objects; cars; and potentially implants.
WHY: It creates a physical world vulnerable to hacking; glitches; and remote shutdowns.

WHAT: The full migration of network functions into software running in data centers.
HOW: It replaces dedicated hardware with code that can be updated or changed instantly from afar.
WHY: It makes critical infrastructure entirely dependent on the stability of commercial cloud providers.

WHAT: Massive clusters of antennas placed in extremely close proximity to users.
HOW: It beams high-frequency signals directly from street furniture or indoor wallpapers.
WHY: It dramatically increases the density of electromagnetic exposure in public and private spaces.

WHAT: The turning of human connection into a tradeable digital asset.
HOW: It uses automated auctions to sell network slices to the highest bidder in real-time.
WHY: It risks creating a tiered society where reliable communication is a luxury product.

WHAT: The network's ability to understand the user's exact situation and environment.
HOW: It harvests data from microphones; GPS; and sensors to build a profile of your current activity.
WHY: It strips away the context of privacy; allowing corporations to monetize your intimate moments.

WHAT: A network management system that operates without any human intervention.
HOW: It detects and fixes issues using black-box AI algorithms that humans cannot audit.
WHY: It creates a "runaway" system where errors or biases can propagate faster than humans can stop them.

WHAT: A layer of processing power embedded directly into the network transmission nodes.
HOW: It forces user data to be processed on the network's computers rather than the user's private device.
WHY: It erodes data sovereignty by forcing processing to happen on infrastructure you do not own.
